Before issuing "DONE", I will verify that for every room I have visited, every available direction has either been traversed or confirmed to lead to a previously visited room. Specifically, when I return to the Kitchen with "south" and "east" available, I will check if "east" has been tried; if not, I will execute "GO: east" instead of stopping. I will only declare "DONE" when I am in a room where all available directions lead to rooms I have already fully explored.

New plan: I failed because I declared "DONE" while in the Kitchen without verifying that all directions from *every* visited room had been exhausted. Specifically, I missed that the "north" direction from the Solarium (visited earlier) was never taken, and I assumed returning to the Kitchen meant the map was fully explored. My previous strategy lacked a systematic check of untried directions in previously visited rooms. Next time, I will maintain a strict mental log of "Room: [Directions Tried]". Before issuing "DONE", I will scan this log to ensure no direction from any visited room remains untried. If I am in a room where all directions are exhausted, I will backtrack to the nearest room in my log that has an untried direction (e.g., if Solarium has "north" untried, I will navigate back to Solarium and execute "GO: north") rather than stopping prematurely. I will only declare "DONE" when the log confirms every available direction from every visited room has been traversed.
